deliverables: Ongoing maintenance: bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, releases
Dijkstra developer preview with initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library
Improved interfaces and documentation for JS/TS components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Runtime foundational components and reactive workers
Dijkstra ledger rules and transaction-builder updates including new builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, and guard scripts
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor
Cleaner integration paths with Cardano Java stack including CCL and Yaci
Runtime chain follower and task scheduler
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability across JVM and JS/TS ecosystems, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is described as an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal states that Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
The proposal states that Scalus components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The document reports three years of development with 4,642 commits, 32 releases, 12 contributors, and more than 20,000 monthly Scalus.js downloads.
The proposal asks for ₳2,464,844 over 9 months, equivalent to about $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate, with no contingency.
The proposal says the current request is reduced from a prior ₳8,503,000 12-month proposal to about ₳2,464,844 over 9 months, with FTE reduced from 8.25 to 2.25 and FTE-months from 99 to 20.25.
The proposal excludes a standalone production-grade JVM L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.
The proposal states delivery will be milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.

The proposal claims Dijkstra hard-fork readiness is needed because Plutus V4 support, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts affect smart contract development, Plutus evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and developer workflows.
The proposal claims Scalus contributes to Cardano 2030 outcomes indirectly by improving developer infrastructure rather than directly generating TVL, transactions, or users.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, emphasizing maintenance of existing infrastructure, Dijkstra readiness, JVM and JS/TS interoperability, and a scoped runtime, with claimed adoption across Cardano protocols and developer tooling plus milestone-based governance controls.
